name: malformed
description:
Nulls where the API documents objects, plus records missing keys entirely. snapshot, cvss, severity_details, related_scanner_findings and vulnerability_root_cause_analysis all arrive as JSON null on one investigation and are simply absent on another; a related finding carries no asset_name, so it falls back to the scanner_finding_hash asset. This is the null-vs-missing distinction that a bare `.get(k, {})` default does NOT cover -- Maze reads through coerce (as_dict/text) and survives, and this scenario is the regression test for that guard.

The short-hash investigation's scanner_finding_hash has no `::` separators at all, so it carries no asset segment and is skipped and logged. The data array also carries a bare string and a null where investigation objects are documented -- both are skipped with a print, never a raise -- and one investigation's related_scanner_findings and vulnerability_root_cause_analysis lists carry stray non-object members that dicts() drops.

The last investigation's cve_id is a vendor advisory code, not a CVE. The platform rejects a Vulnerability whose cve field is not CVE-shaped and fails the WHOLE record, so the code is screened before assignment: the asset still imports, the finding keeps the raw code as its name and maze_cve_id attribute, and its numeric-string base_score and float version exercise the coercion.

namespaced_ids is skipped: Maze ids are bare scanner-supplied names with no tenant scope. Under no-id-match they no longer drive matching.

log_contains: Skipped 3 investigations that named no asset
maze: skipping investigation with no asset name or asset segment: id=inv-short-hash scanner_finding_hash=no-separators-at-all
maze: skipping non-object investigation record: just-a-string-not-an-investigation
